# Neon Plaza (movie billboard demo)

A short walk through a city at night. A big screen on the plaza plays a movie of your own choosing, and the sound of
the movie comes from the screen as 3D sound: it gets louder as you walk up to it and moves between your ears as you
turn.

It shows `GetMovieTexture` (the movie as a texture on a quad), `EmitMovie` (the movie's sound from an entity),
`MovieChannel` with `ChannelRadius` (a wide sound source), and `PlayMovie`, `PauseMovie`, `SeekMovie`, `LoopMovie`
and `MovieVolume`.

## Your movie

The demo plays the first of these that exists:

1. The path given on the command line, for example `movie-billboard.exe "D:\Videos\trailer.mp4"`.
2. The first movie file in the `data` folder next to the program, in name order. When blitzcc runs the program
   straight away (no `-o`), the program is built in a temp folder, so the `data` folder of the current directory
   (the folder of the `.bb` file when started from an editor) is tried next. The file name does not matter, only
   the extension: `.mp4`, `.m4v`, `.mov`, `.mkv`, `.webm`, `.avi`, `.mpg`, `.mpeg`, `.ts`, `.wmv`, `.ogv` or `.flv`.
3. Nothing: the screen shows a test pattern and hums, so the demo still runs.

So after compiling, the folder looks like this:

```
movie-billboard/
  movie-billboard.exe
  data/
    my-trailer.mp4      <- your movie
```

The screen is 24 units wide; its height follows the movie (16:9 gives 13.5). The movie loops unless "Loop the movie"
is off in the options. Which codecs play is listed under [OpenMovie](../../../tools/wiki/text/BlitzBasic/Movies/OpenMovie.md).

## Controls

| Input | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Mouse | Look around |
| W A S D | Walk |
| Shift | Run |
| P | Pause or play the movie |
| R | Play the movie from the start |
| Escape | Pause menu |

The options (mouse speed, invert mouse, field of view, movie volume, looping) are saved in `movie-billboard.cfg`
next to the program.
